correctness.rationale: Binet bounds give a strict explicit lower comparison for the derivative numerator on the new range. A fresh independent execution of the exact interval algorithm checked every width-\(10^{-3}\) subinterval of \([2.23,15]\) at \(\tau=212.435\); the smallest certified lower endpoint was about \(2.293\times10^{-7}\). The tail polynomial and its first derivative are negative at 15 while its second derivative stays negative, forcing the required concavity sign thereafter and hence positivity of the comparison function. The published parameter comparison propagates positivity to smaller \(\tau\). At \(x=9\), fresh directed interval evaluation gave opposite derivative signs at the two quoted endpoints, and parameter monotonicity makes the zero unique. The finite interval computation verifies exactly the compact piece it is claimed to certify; the rest is analytic.
residual_risks: The interval certificate is computer-assisted rather than formally proof-assistant checked.

final_claim: For \(u_\tau(x)=\log\Gamma(x)/\log((x^2+\tau)/(x+\tau))\) with the continuous value at \(x=1\), strict increase holds for every \(0<\tau\le212.435\), while the explicit \(x=9\) derivative obstruction occurs at a unique \(\tau_9\in(212.508612771,212.508612772)\), so the critical parameter lies in the stated interval.
limitations: The exact transition parameter and endpoint behavior remain open; the compact-range proof uses rigorous interval arithmetic rather than a formal proof assistant.
